body: When you get the keys at closing, you rarely know how many copies were made over the years or who still has them. Former owners, neighbors, housekeepers, contractors, and real estate agents may all have had access at some point. A quick key audit before settling in gives you a clear picture of your situation and helps you decide whether rekeying is the right call.
What Is a New Home Key Audit in Belleview, FL?

A key audit is a structured review of every key that provides access to your home. It goes beyond counting what the seller handed you at closing. The goal is to map out every entry point, every lock type, and every person who may have received a copy during the previous owner's time in the house. Start by walking the property and listing every exterior door, garage access point, and any secondary entry like a back gate or storage unit. Then ask the seller or their agent to account for all copies they are aware of. From there, you can decide which locks need attention and which are fine to leave in place.
How Do You Track Who Has Copies of Your Keys?
Tracking key copies is simpler than it sounds when you break it down by category. Think about who typically receives copies during a home's ownership history:

• Family members and trusted neighbors kept for emergencies
  • House cleaners, pet sitters, or property managers
  • Contractors who worked on the property over the years
  • Previous tenants if the home was ever used as a rental

Create a simple written or digital list organized by person and entry point. For each door, mark whether you are confident all copies are accounted for. If there is any gap in that chain, that lock is a candidate for rekeying. Key duplication is fast and inexpensive, which means previous occupants could have made extras at any hardware store without the owner ever knowing. That reality is exactly why an audit matters.
When Is Rekeying Worth It After Moving In?

Rekeying is worth it any time you cannot fully account for existing key copies. It is also the right move if the previous owner was a landlord, if the home was vacant for an extended period, or if the property had multiple people coming and going during a renovation or sale. Lock rekeying is typically more affordable than a full lock replacement and delivers the same result: the old keys no longer work, and only the new set you hold will open the locks.

One Belleview customer moving into a home she inherited had no record of existing key copies. We arrived within the hour, rekeyed all entry points to a single key, and she walked away knowing exactly who had access. Rekeying is smart even when you trust the seller completely. It is not about suspicion. It is about starting fresh with full control over your own home.
Should You Rekey or Replace the Locks Entirely?

Rekeying changes the internal pin configuration of your existing lock so that old keys no longer function. It is the faster and less expensive option, and it works well when the lock hardware itself is in good condition. Lock replacement makes more sense when the locks are worn, outdated, damaged, or you want to upgrade to a higher-security option.
During your key audit, check each lock for these warning signs:

• Stiff or difficult operation even with the correct key
  • Visible corrosion or physical damage to the hardware
  • Difficulty latching or locking consistently
  • Outdated hardware that lacks pick or bump resistance

If the hardware is solid and the only concern is key distribution, rekeying is a clean and cost-effective solution. Our residential locksmith services cover both options, and we can assess each lock on-site to give you a clear recommendation without pushing unnecessary upgrades.
What About Smart Locks as Part of Your New Home Audit?

Some homeowners use a new home audit as the right moment to evaluate whether a smart lock makes sense for their property. Smart locks eliminate the key distribution problem for day-to-day access. You can assign unique codes to family members or service providers and revoke them instantly without calling a locksmith. Smart lock installation works best as a deliberate upgrade on your primary entry, paired with rekeyed locks on secondary doors. The combination gives you flexibility at the front door and tight physical control everywhere else.
Starting Fresh with Full Control Over Your Belleview Home

A new home key audit in Belleview, FL does not have to be complicated. Walk the perimeter, list every lock, account for every copy you can trace, and flag the gaps. Any entry point with an unresolved key history is a candidate for rekeying, and any lock that is worn or outdated is a candidate for replacement. Taking both steps shortly after closing means you move in with complete confidence that old keys are no longer a factor.
